title: Pizzas to plates
hook: Three pizzas, four hungry people, no leftovers. How much does each person get?

knows: a quarter is one of four equal parts

misconception: 3/4 and 3 ÷ 4 are different kinds of things.
objective: The learner can explain that sharing 3 things equally among 4 gives 3/4 of a thing each, so a fraction is a division.

claims.text: Sharing 3 pizzas equally among 4 people is the division 3 ÷ 4, and that is the fraction 3/4.
claims.source: Definition: a/b means a ÷ b (the quotient of a by b). Equal slices assumed on stage.

claims.text: 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75, and 4 people each getting 0.75 of a pizza use 4 × 0.75 = 3 pizzas.
Cutting each of 3 pizzas into 4 equal quarters makes 12 quarters, and dealing one quarter of each pizza to each person gives every person 3 quarters, which is 3/4 of a pizza.
claims.source: 3 x 4 = 12 quarters; 12 / 4 people = 3 each; 3 quarters = 3/4 of a pizza. Stage deals pizza by pizza (Demo.tsx PIZZAS, PEOPLE, PARTS).

claims.text: 4/3 of a pizza is more than a whole pizza, so 4 people could not each get 4/3 from only 3 pizzas.
claims.source: 4 x 4/3 = 5 1/3 pizzas needed, more than 3. Quoted only if the learner chose that option.

claims.text: 1/4 of a pizza is one slice when a pizza is cut into 4 equal slices.
claims.source: Definition of the unit fraction 1/4. Quoted only if the learner chose that option.

recall.question: 5 chocolate bars are shared equally among 8 children. Each child gets...
recall.why: Sharing 5 among 8 is 5 ÷ 8, which is the fraction 5/8. 8/5 would be more than a whole bar each.
